verdict: Okta grew revenue 11% and posted a solid GAAP profit, as subscription sales rose and costs stayed disciplined.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Companies pay per user for Okta's identity tools — single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and governing what AI agents and employees can access.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help with setting Okta up and training — a shrinking line as Okta shifts this work to partners.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the identity platform and new AI-agent security products.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The sales teams and marketing that win and expand customers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal, HR and executives.

otherDetail: Interest income and other income of $19M, net — interest expense was effectively zero after Okta repaid its remaining 2026 convertible notes in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Growth steadied, backlog accelerated
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 11% to $805M. Subscription backlog due within a year (cRPO) grew 14% — faster than revenue — pointing to steadier growth ahead.

takeaways.title: A real GAAP operating margin now
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was $107M, a 13% margin, up from 6% a year ago. Stock-based pay is still large ($114M in the quarter) but shrinking as a share of revenue.

takeaways.title: Cash flow is the standout
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $227M — 28 cents of every revenue dollar — and Okta ended the quarter with $2.3B of cash and short-term investments.

footerNote: Okta's fiscal year ends Jan 31 — this is Q2 FY27, its latest reported quarter (Q3 FY27 due Dec 2026).
follow100Note: GAAP figures throughout. Non-GAAP operating income was $226M, which excludes $114M of stock-based compensation.
